window.note: "Next morning by daylight we were on the march again ... Here a call was made": the morning of 2 July; no hour is stated

place.text: near a farm-house and barn on what Sweitzer took to be the right of the line (the division massed there)

quote: Here a call was made for a regiment from this brigade for picket duty by General Barnes, and Colonel Guiney, with the Ninth Massachusetts, was directed to report to him for instructions, and did so.
context_quote: Next morning by daylight we were on the march again, the Second Brigade leading.
notes: Colonel Sweitzer's account of how the Ninth Massachusetts came to be on picket duty on 2 July (Barnes: detailed "as skirmishers, and deployed at some distance in front of the line"). Strength of the detail not stated (a regiment).

unit_text: the Second Brigade (Sweitzer) with the division

window.part_of_day: until late in the afternoon ("a few hours' quiet and rest")
window.note: after the moves of the morning; no hour is stated (Sweitzer: "the precise time I do not remember"); day bounds, no hour invented (DD-LIFE-02)

place.text: massed in an orchard on the hill above the bridge on the Gettysburg turnpike (the Baltimore pike; the creek crossed by the bridge)

quote: There we remained until late in the afternoon (the precise time I do not remember), and the command had a few hours' quiet and rest.
context_quote: then moved by the front across the creek, and massed in an orchard on the hill above the bridge on the Gettysburg turnpike
notes: Sweitzer's words for what Barnes calls "held in reserve in an orchard on the left of the road": the same halt seen from the Second Brigade. "Meanwhile there had been very little firing along the line".

unit_text: the Ninth Massachusetts (Col. Guiney)

window.part_of_day: all day, until after the fight
window.note: "absent all day on detached duty" (the picket duty called for in the morning) until "shortly afterward" the brigade re-formed after the fight; no hour is stated

place.text: detached from the brigade (picket line; place not stated)

quote: we were shortly afterward joined by the Ninth Massachusetts, which had been absent all day on detached duty
context_quote: (the Ninth Massachusetts being still absent on picket duty)
notes: The regiment on picket (Sweitzer says "still absent on picket duty" when the brigade formed in the afternoon) rejoined after the action of 2 July.

unit_text: the Second Brigade (Sweitzer)

window.part_of_day: from about dark on the 2d to the evening of the 5th
window.note: "About dark on the evening of the 2d" the order came and the brigade was placed; "we remained until the evening of the 5th": the bounds are the sunsets of the two days by the project ephemeris, no hour is stated

place.text: on the right of the First Brigade, left rear of the army's line (the position indicated by Sykes's order)

quote: I received the order, and put the Second Brigade in the position indicated, where we remained until the evening of the 5th, when the division advanced toward Emmitsburg.
context_quote: About dark on the evening of the 2d, the acting assistant adjutantgeneral of the First Brigade came to me
notes: Three nights in one position (2-3, 3-4, 4-5 July) for the Second Brigade; the report states the stay, not camp work, meals or the picket of the position. The field return of 4 July (544 present for duty against 1,010 before the action) is in the inclosure.

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.note: "June 28." heads the entry; no hour

place.text: in camp near Frederick City, Md.

quote: June 28. — In camp near Frederick City.
notes: Itinerary of the Third Brigade, Col. Rice, 14 Aug. 1863 (supplementary to the battle report).

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.part_of_day: camped at 7 p. m.
window.note: "Camped at 7 a. m. [p. m.]": the bracket is in the printed report (the editors' correction); the next entry has the camp left at 4 a. m. on the 30th

place.text: 2 miles beyond Liberty, Md., on the road toward Johnsville

quote: June 29. — Left camp in the morning, and marched 2 miles beyond Liberty, in the direction of Johnsville. Camped at 7 a. m. [p. m.]
notes: Barnes (OR27-1-R189): the division, "passing beyond that place about 2 miles, bivouacked for the night"; Sykes: the corps encamped in the vicinity of Liberty. The hour 7 p. m. is the brigade's own.

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.part_of_day: bivouacked for the night
window.note: arrived "about 4 p. m." and bivouacked for the night; the next entry, "July 1. — Broke camp at 6 a. m.", ends it

place.text: Union Mills, Md.

quote: June 30. — Left camp at 4 a. m., arriving at Union Mills about 4 p. m., when we bivouacked for the night.
notes: Barnes: the enemy cavalry had left Union Mills "some three or four hours before our arrival" and the division "halted here for the night". Sykes: the corps encamped on Big Pipe Creek.

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.part_of_day: at Hanover, about 3 to 5 p. m.
window.note: arrived "about 3 p. m." and "Left again at 5 [p. m.]" (the bracket is in the printed report)

place.text: Hanover, Pa.

quote: arriving at Hanover about 3 p. m. Left again at 5 [p. m.J
context_quote: July 1. — Broke camp at 6 a. m.
notes: The stay at Hanover: what the men did there is not stated here (Chamberlain: rations issued and supper begun, OR27-1-R196). Barnes puts the division's arrival at about 4 p. m.; Sykes has the corps resuming the march at 7 p. m.: conflict C-HANOVER-1JUL. The printed "5 [p. m.J" is read as 5 p. m.

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.part_of_day: bivouacked at 1 a. m.
window.note: "arrived within 3 miles of Gettysburg at 1 a. m. [July 2], when we bivouacked" (the bracket is in the printed report); the next entry, "July 2. — Started at 4 a. m.", ends it

place.text: within 3 miles of Gettysburg on the road from Hanover

quote: and arrived within 3 miles of Gettysburg at 1 a. m. [July 2], when we bivouacked.
context_quote: July 1. — Broke camp at 6 a. m.
notes: Hour and distance of the bivouac of 1-2 July differ between the reports of Sykes (midnight, Bonaughtown), Barnes (after midnight, about 2 miles), Sweitzer (after 12 p. m., 4 or 5 miles) and Rice (1 a. m., within 3 miles): conflict C-BIVOUAC-1JUL.

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.part_of_day: from the start at 4 a. m. to the order at about 4 p. m.
window.note: "Started at 4 a. m." and "awaiting orders until about 4 p. m."; "remained some 2 hours" in the first position (about 2 miles on), then across the creek: the bounds are the two stated clocks

place.text: first about 2 miles from the bivouac (a position taken up), then across the creek (Rock Creek), awaiting orders

quote: Started at 4 a. m.; went about 2 miles, when we got into position; remained some 2 hours; then crossed the creek, and lay in position awaiting orders until about 4 p. m.
context_quote: July 2. — Started at 4 a. m.
notes: The Third Brigade's day of waiting on 2 July before it was ordered to the front: Barnes's "held in reserve in an orchard on the left of the road" and Sweitzer's "a few hours' quiet and rest" are the division-level words for the same hours.

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.part_of_day: during the night
window.note: "that night" after the fight of 2 July: from sunset to sunrise by the project ephemeris; no hour

place.text: on the field of the fight, the left of the line (Little Round Top)

quote: held that position, and bivouacked on the* field that night.
context_quote: July 2. — Started at 4 a. m.
notes: "bivouacked on the* field that night" (the asterisk is in the print) with the dead and wounded of the fight; Rice says in the main report that his men gathered up the wounded and the prisoners before 9 p. m.

unit_text: the prisoners of the brigade (Confederate prisoners taken by the Third Brigade)

window.part_of_day: morning
window.note: "The following morning" after the fight of 2 July; no hour is stated

place.text: the ground of the brigade on the left of the line (Little Round Top and the ground in front)

quote: The following morning the prisoners of the brigade buried all of our own dead and a large nuinber of those of the enemy.
context_quote: had taken and sent to the rear over 500 prisoners
notes: Colonel Rice 31 July 1863: prisoners buried the Union dead and many Confederate dead on 3 July. The report says over 500 prisoners were taken and sent to the rear; how many were set to this work, with what tools and where the graves were is not stated. Barnes (same brigade, "The following day was principally occupied in burying the dead") is the second statement.

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.part_of_day: during the fight, about 4 to 8 p. m.
window.note: the brigade was "ordered into position at about 4 p. m. of the 2d instant"; the report puts the end of the fight at "8 o'clock in the evening": the ammunition came between

place.text: the brigade's line on Little Round Top (ammunition brought from the rear and distributed along the line)

quote: I sent four of them, one after another, with orders for ammunition. The ammunition came promptly, was distributed at once, and the fight went on.
context_quote: was detached from the division and ordered into position at about 4 p. m. of the 2d instant
notes: Colonel Chamberlain and other commanders said their commands were out of ammunition; Rice sent four officers "pressed into service" for it; it came "promptly" and "was distributed at once". Who carried it and in what, and how much, is not stated. Barnes (OR27-1-R189) says the 20th Maine "replenished it from the cartridgeboxes of the men lying around them".

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.note: the supplementary report has the brigade on the field "until about 9 a. m., when we were relieved by the First Brigade and Ninth Massachusetts"; "the balance of the day" in reserve: the end is the day bound

place.text: in reserve at "the center of the line" (the supplementary report: "their old position farther to the right")

quote: The brigade was relieved during the forenoon of the 3d instant by the First Brigade, and ordered tb the center of the line, where it remained in reserve the balance of the day, exposed to a severe cannonading
context_quote: Remained on the field of the previous day's fight until about 9 a. m., when we were relieved by the First Brigade and Ninth Massachusetts, of the Second Brigade
notes: (The print has "tb" for "to".) The brigade lay in reserve during the cannonade of 3 July "with no loss, from the security of its position". The main report says the center of the line; the supplementary report says "we taking their old position farther to the right" (the Second Brigade's): the two wordings may describe the same ground.

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.part_of_day: bivouacked about 10 p. m.
window.note: "Bivouacked on the road about 10 p. m."; the next entry, "July 6. — Started at 6 a. m.", ends it

place.text: on the road toward Emmitsburg, Md. (about 5 hours' march from the field)

quote: July 5. — Same position as previous day. Started about 5 p. m. in direction of Emmitsburg. Bivouacked on the road about 10 p. m.

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.part_of_day: camped about noon
window.note: "arrived at 12 m. [noon] ... when we camped"; the next entry, "July 7. — Left camp about 6 a. m.", ends it

place.text: within 3 miles of Emmitsburg, Md.

quote: July 6. — Started at 6 a. m., and arrived at 12 m. within 3 miles of Emmitsburg, when we camped.
notes: A day camp in rain (the weather of the retreat is not stated in this passage); camp layout and meals not stated.

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.part_of_day: bivouacked at 6 p. m.
window.note: "at 6 p. m., when we bivouacked"; the next entry, "July 8. — Broke camp early in the morning", gives no hour and the project ephemeris ends on 6 July (sun events are not available for the 7th and 8th), so the end is the day bound

place.text: within 5 miles of Frederick City, Md.

quote: July 7. — Left camp about 6 a. m., and arrived within 5 miles of Frederick City at 6 p. m., when we bivouacked.

unit_text: the Eighty-third Pennsylvania (Capt. Woodward)

window.note: arrived at Jones' Cross-Roads "about 3 p. m." and "went on picket immediately"; the relief is not stated, so the end is the day bound

place.text: at Jones' Cross-Roads, Md.

quote: The Eighty-third Pennsylvania went on picket immediately.
context_quote: July 10. — Broke camp early in the morning, and arrived at Jones' Cross-Roads about 3 p. m.
notes: One regiment on picket on arrival (3 p. m. 10 July); the strength of the detail is not stated.

unit_text: the Third Brigade (Rice)

window.note: "July 13." heads the entry; no hour

place.text: in front of the Hagerstown and Sharpsburg pike, Md.

quote: Camped in front of pike
context_quote: July 13. — Camped in front of pike; two companies of the Eightythird Pennsylvania on picket.
notes: The camp lay in front of the pike on the Hagerstown and Sharpsburg road (the line had "advanced on" it the day before).

unit_text: two companies of the Eighty-third Pennsylvania

window.note: "July 13." heads the entry; no hour

place.text: in front of the camp at the pike (Hagerstown and Sharpsburg pike), Md.

quote: two companies of the Eightythird Pennsylvania on picket.
context_quote: July 13. — Camped in front of pike
notes: Two companies detailed for picket: the number of men is not stated (the passage gives companies, not men).

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.part_of_day: just before sunset (sunset 19:32 local mean time on 1 July by the project ephemeris)
window.note: "just before sunset on that day" is the arrival at Hanover; the issue was begun after it; no hour is stated and none is invented (DD-LIFE-02)

place.text: Hanover, Pa.

quote: Rations were scarcely issued
context_quote: on reaching Hanover, Pa., just before sunset on that day
notes: Chamberlain, report of 6 July 1863: the regiment, advance guard of the march, reached Hanover "just before sunset"; rations had "scarcely" been issued when the order to march came. Barnes has the division arriving at about 4 p. m. and Rice the brigade at about 3 p. m. (conflict C-HANOVER-1JUL). The seed row of the planning step for this passage is replaced by this and the two rows that follow.

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.part_of_day: just before sunset (sunset 19:32 local mean time on 1 July by the project ephemeris)
window.note: as the ration row: after the arrival "just before sunset", before the order to march; no hour

place.text: Hanover, Pa.

quote: the men about preparing supper
context_quote: on reaching Hanover, Pa., just before sunset on that day
notes: Supper being prepared when the rumour of the fight at Gettysburg came; whether it was eaten is not stated ("orders came to march forthwith"). How and over what fires is not stated.

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.part_of_day: just before sunset (sunset 19:32 local mean time on 1 July by the project ephemeris)
window.note: on reaching Hanover "just before sunset"; the bivouac was not made, the march was ordered; no hour

place.text: Hanover, Pa.

quote: lost no time in getting ready for an. expected bivouac
context_quote: on reaching Hanover, Pa., just before sunset on that day
notes: Preparations for a bivouac that the order to march cut short (the print has "an. expected bivouac").

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.part_of_day: just before daybreak, "an hour or two of sleep by the roadside"
window.note: the bounds are the start of 2 July and the arrival "at about 7 a. m."; the sleep was "just before daybreak" (no hour; civil dawn about 04:03 and sunrise about 04:35 local mean time by the project ephemeris)

place.text: by the roadside on the road from Hanover toward Gettysburg

quote: After an hour or two of sleep by the roadside just before daybreak, we reached the heights southeasterly of Gettysburg at about 7 a. m., July 2.
notes: "an hour or two of sleep by the roadside": the regiment lay down along the road after the night march. The brigade reports give the bivouac as 1 a. m. (Rice), midnight (Sykes) or after midnight (Barnes): conflict C-BIVOUAC-1JUL.

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.part_of_day: the forenoon and the early afternoon of 2 July, in line of battle
window.note: from the arrival "at about 7 a. m." to "Somewhere near 4 p. m." when the cannonade was the signal to move (both in the context quote)

place.text: on the heights south-east of Gettysburg, massed with the division on the right of the road and moved several times toward the left

quote: yet the men were able to take some rest
context_quote: we reached the heights southeasterly of Gettysburg at about 7 a. m., July 2. Massed at first with the rest of the division on the right of the road, we were moved several times farther toward the left. Although expecting every moment to be put into action and held strictly in line of battle, yet the men were able to take some rest and make the most of their rations. Somewhere near 4 p. m. a sharp cannonade
notes: Rest in line of battle ("held strictly in line of battle"), the same hours as Barnes's "held in reserve in an orchard on the left of the road" and Rice's "lay in position awaiting orders until about 4 p. m."

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.part_of_day: during the wait of 2 July
window.note: from the arrival "at about 7 a. m." to "Somewhere near 4 p. m." (the same sentence and the following one): no meal hour is stated

place.text: on the heights south-east of Gettysburg, in line of battle

quote: and make the most of their rations
context_quote: we reached the heights southeasterly of Gettysburg at about 7 a. m., July 2. Massed at first with the rest of the division on the right of the road, we were moved several times farther toward the left. Although expecting every moment to be put into action and held strictly in line of battle, yet the men were able to take some rest and make the most of their rations. Somewhere near 4 p. m. a sharp cannonade
notes: The men ate their rations while waiting in line of battle; what they ate, when and whether they cooked are not stated. The clip (hardtack) is a stand-in for "rations".

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.part_of_day: in the intervals of the fight
window.note: "The intervals of the struggle" between "Somewhere near 4 p. m." and "dusk"; no hour is stated

place.text: in front of and behind the Twentieth Maine's line on Little Round Top

tools_props.item: cartridge boxes of disabled friend or foe

quote: to gather ammunition from the cartridge-boxes of disabled friend or foe on the field
context_quote: Somewhere near 4 p. m. a sharp cannonade, at some distance to our left and front
notes: Cartridges gathered from the boxes of the fallen, and "scanty ammunition snatched from the field" (same page). Barnes (OR27-1-R189) retells it from the brigade reports.

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.part_of_day: during the night after the advance at 9 p. m.
window.note: after "It was now 9 p. m." (the advance up the mountain) to the sunrise bound of the project ephemeris; "during the night": no hour of the posting

place.text: to the front of the position on the crest of Great Round Top (the western slope of the hill seized at 9 p. m.)

quote: sent a strong picket to the front, with instructions to report to me every half hour during the night
context_quote: Colonel Rice then directed me to make the movement to seize that crest. It was now 9 p. m.
notes: (The print has "1 /sent" for "I sent".) A strong picket (the number is not stated) with a report every half hour; the 83rd Pennsylvania and the 44th New York had come up and were posted.

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.part_of_day: during the night after the advance at 9 p. m.
window.note: after "It was now 9 p. m." to the sunrise bound; no hour is stated

place.text: on the crest of Great Round Top, among the rocks

quote: allowed the rest of my men tcj sleep on their arms
context_quote: Colonel Rice then directed me to make the movement to seize that crest. It was now 9 p. m.
notes: "to sleep on their arms" (the print has "tcj"); the men of the regiment not on picket, a handful of 200 who had made the advance. Fisher's two regiments came up beyond the left about midnight (same report).

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.part_of_day: before the fight (the march of 1-2 July and the morning)
window.note: the passage belongs to the account of the strength going into the fight of 2 July; when they were put under guard is not stated

place.text: with the regiment (place not stated)

quote: Some prisoners I had under guard, under sentence of court-martial, I was obliged to put into the fight
context_quote: We went into the fight with 386, all told — 358 guns.
notes: Men of the regiment under sentence of court-martial were held under guard until the fight and then released into the ranks; the number is not stated.

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.part_of_day: on the march of 1-2 July and in the morning of the fight
window.note: the march of 1-2 July (Hanover to Gettysburg) and the following morning: the sick and foot-sore fell out and came up "as soon as they could find their regiments"; no hour

place.text: the road from Hanover to Gettysburg and the heights south-east of Gettysburg

quote: Even the sick and foot-sore, who could not keep up in the march, came up as soon as they could find their regiments
context_quote: Every pioneer and musician who could carry a musket went into the ranks.
notes: Stragglers of the march rejoined the regiment in line of battle on 2 July; the number is not stated (the regiment went into the fight with 386, all told).

unit_text: my command (the Twentieth Maine, Chamberlain)

window.note: "On the 4th": after a reconnaissance to the front the regiment returned to Little Round Top and buried the dead; no hour

place.text: Little Round Top, where the dead had been laid during the fight; 50 Confederate dead buried in front of the position of 2 July

tools_props.item: head-boards made of ammunition boxes with the soldier's name cut upon each

quote: where we buried our dead in the place where we had laid them during the fight, marking each grave by a head-board made of ammunition boxes, with each dead soldier's name cut upon it. We also buried 50 of the enemy's dead in front of our position of July 2.
context_quote: On the 4th, we made a reconnaissance to the front, to ascertain the movements of the enemy
notes: Chamberlain: the regiment buried its own dead on 4 July where they had been laid during the fight (the report counts 30 killed in the regiment, 136 lost in all) and 50 of the enemy's dead; each grave had a head-board of ammunition boxes with the name cut upon it. Rice (OR27-1-R195) says prisoners buried the brigade's dead on the morning of 3 July; Barnes says the Third Brigade spent 3 July in burying the dead (conflict C-LRT-BURIAL).

unit_text: this regiment (the Twentieth Maine, Capt. Clark)

window.part_of_day: bivouacked at midnight
window.note: "bivouacked at midnight" (00:00 on 6 July); "Early on the morning of the 6th, marched 1 mile": no hour, so the end is the sunrise bound of the project ephemeris

place.text: near Marsh Creek, on the Emmitsburg road (10 miles from the field)

quote: in the direction of Emmitsburg, and bivouacked at midnight near Marsh Creek.
context_quote: this regiment moved forward on the battle-field of Gettysburg, and occupied the Carolina road during the day
notes: (The print has "marclied" for "marched" earlier in the sentence: "At night, marched 10 miles".) The brigade itinerary (Rice, Lamont) has the brigade bivouacking on the road about 10 p. m. on 5 July; Clark has the regiment bivouacking at midnight: conflict C-BIV-0705.

unit_text: this regiment (the Twentieth Maine, Capt. Clark)

window.part_of_day: early on the morning
window.note: "Early on the morning of the 6th": no hour

place.text: one mile on from the bivouac near Marsh Creek (the regiment's field near Emmitsburg, where Chamberlain dated his report on 6 July)

quote: Early on the morning of the 6th, marched 1 mile, and bivouacked.
notes: The brigade itinerary has the brigade marching from 6 a. m. to 12 m. and camping within 3 miles of Emmitsburg on 6 July (conflict C-CAMP-0706).

unit_text: this regiment (the Twentieth Maine, Capt. Clark)

window.note: "on the 7th"; the hour of the bivouac is not stated (the brigade itinerary has 6 p. m. within 5 miles of Frederick City)

place.text: 6 miles above Frederick City, Md. (18 miles from the bivouac of the previous night)

quote: Resumed march on the 7th through Creagerstown, and bivouacked 6 miles above Frederick City and 18 miles from bivouac of previous night.
notes: Rice and Lamont: "within 5 miles of Frederick City at 6 p. m., when we bivouacked": the distance differs by a mile (conflict C-BIV-0707).

unit_text: this regiment (the Twentieth Maine, Capt. Clark)

window.part_of_day: in the afternoon, in heavy rain
window.note: "in the afternoon": no hour (Rice and Lamont: arrived at Middletown about 4 p. m.)

place.text: near Middletown, Md.

quote: On the 8th, moved in heavy rain 13 miles across the Catoctin Mountains, and encamped near Middletown in the afternoon.
notes: Heavy rain on 8 July (the regiment moved 13 miles in it before encamping); camp layout not stated.

unit_text: this regiment (the Twentieth Maine, Capt. Clark)

window.part_of_day: in the afternoon
window.note: "in the afternoon": no hour (Rice and Lamont: within 2 miles of Boonsborough "about noon")

place.text: near Boonsborough, Md. (8 miles from Middletown)

quote: and encamped near Boonsborough in the afternoon, 8 miles from
context_quote: On the morning of the 9th, the regiment crossed over South Mountain
notes: Clark: the afternoon; the brigade itinerary: about noon (the two are not in conflict if noon is early afternoon).

unit_text: this regiment (the Twentieth Maine, Capt. Clark)

window.note: "The regiment moved early on the day following" the 9th: 10 July; the hours of the skirmish line are not stated

place.text: on the Sharpsburg pike near Jones' Cross-Roads, Md.

quote: in the vicinity of the enemy, on the Sharpsburg pike, near Jones' Cross-Roads, was thrown forward to act as skirmishers.
context_quote: The regiment moved early on the day following
notes: A skirmish line that was "soon warmly engaged" and "after a severe and protracted skirmish, held the pike" (2 killed and 6 wounded and missing): a picket line that became an action, not a camp picket.

unit_text: this regiment (the Twentieth Maine, Capt. Clark)

window.note: "On the 11th"; the hour is not stated

place.text: 2 miles along the pike and westward from Jones' Cross-Roads, Md.

quote: On the 11th, the regiment moved along the pike and westward, through field and wood, 2 miles, and bivouacked.

unit_text: this regiment (the Twentieth Maine, Capt. Clark)

window.note: "On the morning of the 13th, advanced to the Williamsport road, and the next day": 14 July; no hour

place.text: beyond the Williamsport road, Md.

quote: threw forward pickets. On the 14th, marched to Williamsport
context_quote: On the morning of the 13th, advanced to the Williamsport road, and the next day
notes: (The print has "ci^ossed" for "crossed": "the next day crossed the Williamsport road and threw forward pickets".) Pickets thrown forward by the regiment on 14 July; strength not stated. The regiment marched to Williamsport the same day.

unit_text: the regiment (the Sixteenth Michigan, Lieut. Col. Welch)

window.part_of_day: during most of the day, until about 4 p. m.
window.note: "during most of the day" before "About 4 p. m. we moved rapidly to the extreme left": the end is the stated 4 p. m., the start is the day bound

place.text: near and in rear of Gettysburg, to the left of the main road (the heights south-east of the town)

quote: lay with the Third Brigade, First Division, Fifth Corps, closed in mass, near and in rear of Gettysburg, to the left of the main road
context_quote: About 4 p. m. we moved rapidly to the extreme left of our line of battle
notes: The regiment lay "closed in mass" with the brigade through the day of 2 July; no meal, fire or sleep is mentioned here (Chamberlain says the men of the 20th Maine "took some rest and made the most of their rations").

unit_text: the regiment (the Sixteenth Michigan, Lieut. Col. Welch)

window.note: "On the 3d" the regiment took up a new line and "remained on our arms for twenty-four hours": from some hour on 3 July for 24 hours (into 4 July)

place.text: a new line farther to the right, on the left of the brigade (3 July)

window.note: "In the darkness of tlie night" after the fight of the afternoon of 2 July: the night of 2-3 July, sunset to sunrise by the project ephemeris; no hour

place.text: the eastern slope of Little Round Top, beneath the trees where the dead lay

quote: Grouped by companies, a row of inanimate forms lay side by side beneath the trees upon this eastern slope. No funeral ceremony, and only shallow graves could be accorded them. In the darkness of tlie night, silently and with bitter dejection, each company buried its dead.
notes: Dedication address for the 140th New York, New York at Gettysburg (1902), vol. 3: spoken decades after the event. Each company buried its own dead in shallow graves in the dark after the fight (the address gives 26 killed and 85 enlisted men and 6 officers wounded for the regiment; tools and the number of burying men are not stated). Conflict C-LRT-BURIAL concerns the burying of the Confederate dead and the wider burials (3-4 July).

unit_text: the regiment (the 146th New York), told by Lieut. A. P. Case

window.part_of_day: from about 6 a. m. until "About 3 p. m."
window.note: "reached the Gettysburg field about 6 a. m., July 2d, and was stationed" and, in the context quote, "About 3 p. m., the Fifth Corps was ordered in to support General Sickles"

place.text: the west side of Rock Creek, near the bridge on the Baltimore Pike, on the extreme right of the Union line

tier_basis: The account says the corps "was stationed" there from about 6 a. m. until it was ordered to the left at about 3 p. m. (a wait of nine hours); that the men rested is reasoned from the wait (Garrard: "idle, lying by their arms until about 4 p. m."; Chamberlain: "the men were able to take some rest").
quote: The Fifth Corps, after marching nearly all night, reached the Gettysburg field about 6 a. m., July 2d, and was stationed on the west side of Rock Creek, near the bridge on the Baltimore Pike, on the extreme right of the Union line.
context_quote: About 3 p. m., the Fifth Corps was ordered in to support General Sickles, who held the extreme left of the Union line.
notes: Account by Lieut. A. P. Case (146th New York), "The taking and holding of Little Round Top", New York at Gettysburg (1902), vol. 3: written decades after the event. Arrival on the field "about 6 a. m." (Case, "after marching nearly all night"): conflict C-ARRIVAL-0702 (the 140th New York: shortly after sunrise; Barnes and the 62nd Pennsylvania: about 7 a. m.; Sykes: about 8 a. m.). The ordered move "About 3 p. m." against about 4 p. m. in Sykes, Barnes and Garrard.
